drafted_from: tool:answer-a-checks-questions-with-a-model-on-this-computer row in tools/ask-a-small-model-for-a-verdict/tool-rows.json, its code in tools/ask-a-small-model-for-a-verdict/do-work/ and tools/ask-a-small-model-for-a-verdict/test/answer-with-a-downloaded-model.test.mjs, its row's verify sample run and do-work/answer_with_a_downloaded_model.py; the answers were produced by running the tool against a stand-in model server
start_here: Say to your AI: "Answer the is-this-line-vague question for the line 'Things happen.' and for 'The kettle boils in two minutes.' with my answering settings." It runs the answerer and gives each line's probability for no and yes.

lists.label: Checks
lists.holds: One node of a person's check tree per row; the rows these tools read are labelled lines (kind labelled-line: a line of copy with the person's ruling, good or bad, and the set it belongs to) and check rows with an ask (a question for a model).
alike: a spreadsheet of example lines marked good or bad
the labelled examples of a style guide
a test set of sentences with pass or fail

instructions: 1. Have your setting row (record:setting:ask-a-small-model-for-a-verdict~person~sample-person: batch sizes, the frame the line is shown in, good_sets, fit bars, and where answers are cached) and your ruled lines in list:checks (pour the example rows into your own list, or add rows of kind labelled-line).

2. Take the questions from tool:check-against-a-persons-rules-and-verdicts: each is {question, options, text} with the check row's model ({mlx}, {consult}, {stand_in}) or adapter, and optional examples {items: <set>, bad_for} and context.

3. Say "Answer my check's questions". The AI calls tools:run with this tool, settings_record and asks (the worked example shows one); mode "live" asks a model for what the answer cache lacks, "cache" answers only from it.
4. Read result: one {option: probability} per ask, in order, or null where nothing could answer. Every answer is kept, so a line is never asked twice.

worked_examples.title: Two lines answered by a stand-in model: the vague one scores yes 0.9
worked_examples.ask: Answer my check's vague-line question for these two lines.

asks.question: Is this line vague?
asks.text: The kettle boils in two minutes.

worked_examples.given: From the row's own verify sample run in tools/ask-a-small-model-for-a-verdict/tool-rows.json, answered by running do-work/answer_with_a_downloaded_model.py with the same stand-in: the setting row for person sample-person and four ruled lines in list:checks (set sample-rulings: "Things happen." and "It works somehow." bad for vague; "Ten people came." and "The door is red." good). The stand-in answers each listed text from its own table and every other text with {"no": 0.95, "yes": 0.05}.
worked_examples.hands_back: [{"no": 0.1, "yes": 0.9}, {"no": 0.95, "yes": 0.05}]: the first line is probably vague, the kettle line is not.

pour.how: Name the list you already keep for lines you ruled good or bad and its fields. The tool matches each kit field to one of yours (by the map you give, the same id, the same label, or a name in alike), refuses when fewer than 80% match, and otherwise answers the records:write that adds the example rows, leaving your own rows untouched.
